source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension — trifold "ដំណាំល្ហុង" (Papaya Cultivation), citing Training Module on Fruit Tree Production (2013) and a farmer's field experience from Kampong district, Preah Vihear province (2012)
text:
Farmers are advised to choose and prepare their papaya field about 1 to 1.5 months ahead of planting, to make sure the plot has good, fertile soil. Once the plot is chosen, stretch a straight line across it to make marking planting points easier, and set planting points 3 meters apart in each direction — the source's diagram shows this as a triangular (staggered) spacing pattern rather than a plain square grid.

At each marked point, dig a planting hole and mix in well-decomposed manure — about 500 cc of manure mixed with 20 liters of water — blending it into the soil at the bottom of the hole. Cover the hole back over and let it sit for about 4 days so the manure mixture settles and partially decomposes before the seedling is planted into it.
caveat: The source does not give explicit hole width/depth measurements in the legible body text (only the 3m tree spacing and the manure-mixing quantities are clearly stated); no hole dimensions were invented to fill this gap.
